### The deprecated import route

`POST .../oauth/import-tokens` still works, and is removed
90 days after the\naccounts API shipped. It uploads to your default account, creating an unnamed\none when the server has none, an
d keeps its old body and its old\n`{ imported, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carries `Deprecation: true`, a\n`Sunset` date and

a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An account this route creates is hosted-only. An existing default it writes
into keeps whatever r
ule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the URL saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourc

eUrl`
and `tokens.id_token` are accepted and ignored. Move to
`PUT .../accounts/{account}`, which names the account it writes.
\nThe error codes these routes add to `details.code` are listed in the\n[error code reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshoo

ting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors).

The shortest useful loop: create a run with one inline

": ["'$SERVER_ID'"],

per-iteration tool calls, token usage, latency\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/it

The decision summary composes steps 2 and 4 into one version

ed object so every
client reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gating on it:

* **`measurementUnit` ships with
every count.** Under per-case grading the\n counts are case-execution *variants*, with iterations as trials inside them;\n under
a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are trials. The same suite reports\n a different total under each, 3 against 15 for three c

ases run five times,
 so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never converted
 across that line.
* **It expl
ains the verdict; it never re-decides it.** The run's own decision is\n the authority and is carried through on `decision`. The p
er-trial\n `diagnostics` sit underneath it. A case can pass with a failing trial in it,\n so tallying diagnostics gives a differ
ent answer than the platform reached.\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a failure and not `inconclusive`.** It\n means no
verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.reason` says which. `inconclusive` *is* a decisi

on; the validity
 phase ran and withheld a verdict.
* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether you have the whole list.** A page

fetched with a `cursor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates
 "nothing failed" from "we did not look".
Evidence is scoped to the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span\nids, prompt indexes and reasons come from the first
failed stage's row alone,\nand `evidence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you can append to your base URL\nto read the full trac

e.

`model` takes an id from the hosted catalog (`provider/name` form, e.g.
`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`) and runs on your orga
nization's credits.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pass\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A mod
el the API can't execute is rejected at\ncreate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedModels` lists the valid\nhosted ids f

or that provider.

Reruns are even shorter: `{ "suiteId": "..." }` reruns the suite exactly as
configured, connecting the s
uite's saved server selection (the `202` response\nlists the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverIds` to override the selection; a\ns

uite with no saved selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with
`details.reason: "NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running against a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is launchable only through a suite that has
it *
*attached**. Attach them first with\n`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`\narray (send `nul
l` to detach them all; `[]` is rejected, use `null`), then\npass `environmentId` on the run. It must be one of that suite's attach

ed
environments; anything else is a `400` with
`details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED"`, raised before any case is
author

ed or any server connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depends on the suite:

* **no** attached environments
→ the run uses the saved server selection, as before;\n* **exactly one** attached → that environment is used automatically. The `

naming the candidates.

The environment supplies the closed server set, so `serverIds` is not required and is
**rejected** al
ongside it (`400`), rather than accepted and ignored: honoring\nboth would connect a different set than the run is stamped with. T
he same goes\nfor a `serverIds` override on an environment-based suite\n(`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE\"`

d with `CONFLICT` (409)
rather than executing against a different configuration than the one whose
tools were captured. Use
`GE

T /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` to see what it
will connect before launching.

When creating a ne
w inline suite, `POST .../eval-runs` also accepts `hosts: [{ host: \"Claude\", servers: [\"my-server\"] }]`, using the same host n
ame or ID and optional server selection as `POST .../eval-suites`. A single host is selected for the run automatically. With multi
ple attachments, use `namedHostId` to select the run's client. For an existing suite, update its attachments first. If `hosts` is
omitted, the run uses the project's default client.\n\nRun reads and listings expose `client: { id, name, source, hostStyle?, mode
lId? }` when recorded. `id` is the named host ID or `null`; `source` is `environment`, `attached_host`, `suite_default`, or `sdk`.
The name is durable even if the host is deleted. SDK executions use `SDK harness`; `launcher.client` separately identifies the la
unching process. Older runs without a descriptor omit `client`. `modelSource: \"case\"` means the run's sole model came from its c
ase snapshot; `client_default` and `override` retain their existing meanings.\n\nEvery run records which environment it used. `GET
.../eval-runs/{runId}` (and\nthe run listings) return `environment: { id, name, revision }` (read from the\nrun's immutable snaps

hot, not the suite's current attachments) or `null` for a
run that used a saved server selection.

Per-organization
concurrenc
y is capped (default **2** concurrent runs); exceeding it returns\n`429` with `details.reason: \"CONCURRENT_RUN_LIMIT\"`; wait for

an active run
to finish.

If a server answers `401 OAUTH_REQUIRED`, complete the OAuth flow yourself
(the SDK's `runOAuthLogi
n` handles interactive, headless, and\nclient-credentials flows) and upload the token to one of the server's\n[accounts](#server-a
